scene: Inside the sloop's dark, cramped hold lit by a single shuttered lantern, the Gunner (short, stocky man of about forty-five, shaved head, thick black beard going gray, sleeveless leather jerkin over a gray shirt, powder horn on a cord) lies stretched across a row of wooden gunpowder barrels like a bed, eyes wide open and bloodshot, clutching a blanket, while above him at the hatch Tom (navy waistcoat, no hat) leans down with an unlit clay pipe in his mouth and a curious face. A small sign of crossed-out flame is painted on the nearest barrel (no words). Tension: the man who sleeps on the bomb, and the man who wants to smoke.

On the sloop's deck in bright afternoon sun, the Gunner crouches behind one small black cannon on its wooden carriage, holding a smoking slow match on a stick an inch from the touch-hole, frozen, sweat flying, while the Captain (black tricorn, full brown beard, burgundy long coat) and the Quartermaster (dark-brown wavy hair, white shirt, dark-brown waistcoat) both throw up their mitten hands shouting 'wait' and a merchant ship in the distance is already lowering her sails. A splash from a cannonball rises harmlessly short in the water between the ships. Tension: one shot too many could ruin the prize.
